claim: The peer-reviewed version of Yuqing Xing's iPhone X value-added analysis was published in Frontiers of Economics in China (Higher Education Press), vol. 15(4), pp. 642-658, December 2020, confirming the working paper's findings passed academic peer review rather than remaining an unreviewed working paper.
stance_target: Citability and authority of the $104-value-added / 25% China-share iPhone X figures used elsewhere in this research
quoted_support: Other versions of this item: Yuqing Xing, 2020. "How the iPhone Widens the U.S. Trade Deficit with China: The Case of the iPhone X," Frontiers of Economics in China-Selected Publications from Chinese Universities, Higher Education Press, vol. 15(4), pages 642-658, December.
numbers: Frontiers of Economics in China vol. 15(4), pp. 642-658, Dec 2020

claim: Approximately 45% of the iPhone X's total value added originated from Japan, South Korea, and other non-US, non-China economies -- a larger share than China's own 25% contribution.
stance_target: China is not even the largest source of non-US value-added in the iPhone; Japan/Korea/other collectively exceed it
scope_conditions: iPhone X bill of materials, 2017-2019 analysis
quoted_support: According to the bill of materials, those companies contributed 25% of the value added of the iPhone X. About 45% of the value added of the iPhone X originated from Japan, Korean and other economies.
